NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular business
  hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a recording is
  available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35 (Cox) and
  Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails received
  before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

Relief Fund.

   approve Resolution No. 2563 authorizing execution of a contract with the Los Angeles

  DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM

  JUNE 30, 2023

  Recommendation: That the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates receive
  and file the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) for fiscal year ended

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material), and introduced Demi Hite, CPA, Senior Auditor with Rogers, Anderson, Malody &
Scott, who presented a summary of the FY 2023-2024 audit.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL REPORT
  (ACFR) FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 2023.

There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JANUARY 23, 2024
   COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER,
  TO ADJOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING.

**ADJOURNED TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING**

B.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ANNUAL BOARD OF DIRECTORS MEETING

  Recommendation: That the Rolling Hills Estates Pepper Tree Foundation Board of
  Directors receive and file this report.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

BOARD MEMBER HUFF requested that the report for the conceptual plan for large donations
be included in the final report. BOARD MEMBER HUFF also requested that the 19th
Amendment title be included in the report.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  VICE-CHAIR STEGURA moved, seconded by BOARD MEMBER ZERUNYAN, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE ANNUAL REPORT.

There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  BOARD MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by VICE-CHAIR STEGURA, TO
  RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING.

**RECONVENED TO CITY COUNCIL MEETING**

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037
  COMPREHENSIVE ZONING CODE UPDATE - COMMERCIAL DISTRICT
  LOCATION: CITYWIDE

  Recommendation: That the City Council discuss the issues and provide direction to
  staff as appropriate.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Community Development Director Naughton explained that staff would be proposing a stepped
approach based on street width when it comes to setbacks, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER SCHACHTER.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked staff and appreciates the effort to simplify the code.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA stated that she is in favor of providing more certainty to property
owners and developers, and of getting rid of any discrepancies in the code. Community
Development Director Naughton stated that the process of updating the code will be
incremental, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA encouraged members of the public to participate in the process
of updating the planning codes.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  IT WAS THE CONSENSUS OF THE COUNCIL FOR STAFF TO PROCEED AS
  PRESENTED.

There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JANUARY 23, 2024
 D.  SECOND AMENDMENT TO MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH
  PENINSULA CITIES AND PALOS VERDES PENINSULA UNIFIED SCHOOL
  DISTRICT FOR COST SHARING TWO SCHOOL RESOURCE OFFICERS

  Recommendation: That City Council approve the Second Amendment to the MOU
  between the PVPUSD and the cities of Palos Verdes Estates, Rancho Palos Verdes,
  Rolling Hills, and Rolling Hills Estates for cost sharing two School Resource Officers
  (SROs).

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF stated she supports the contract extension.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA toured Peninsula High School and met with the SRO there.
She stated is hopeful that the Sheriff deputies on the Peninsula feel that the existence of the
SROs allows them to do other things. She also noted that reports of encounters between the
students and SROs are given to the cities for review.

MAYOR SCHMITZ explained that her daughter who is a student at Palos Verdes High School
sees the SROs as part of the staff and administration, and that they are a seamless part of her
school experience.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE MOU BETWEEN THE
  PVPUSD AND THE CITIES OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, RANCHO PALOS
  VERDES, ROLLING HILLS, AND ROLLING HILLS ESTATES FOR COST
  SHARING TWO SCHOOL RESOURCE OFFICERS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

E.  GRANT PROGRAM PARTICIPATION AGREEMENT - BUILDING ELECTRIFICATION
  (REACH) CODE DEVELOPMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize staff to execute the participation
  agreement in CPA’s Reach Code Program.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Community Development Director Naughton confirmed that the Reach Code Program could
help upgrade City Hall’s electric infrastructure to be able to bring super-chargers to City Hall,
in response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN. COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated
that more super-chargers are needed on the Peninsula.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE STAFF TO EXECUTE THE PARTICIPATION AGREEMENT IN
  CPA’S REACH CODE PROGRAM.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JANUARY 23, 2024

  DAY CHANGE

  Recommendation: That the City Council consider the request from the Park and
  Activities Commission and direct staff to return with a Resolution amending the
  Commission's regular meeting day.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Discussion ensued about the process of changing the date/time by Resolution of the City
Council.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.
